title: Trajectory-Aware Clinical Risk Prediction via Severity-Grounded Knowledge Graphs and Retrieval-Augmented Generation

problem.claim: Augmenting patient records with heterogeneous external knowledge to predict clinical risk remains challenging.

gap.claim: Existing methods do not adequately capture disease severity, treatment responses, and nuanced clinical progression because of data sparsity and underuse of unstructured clinical notes.

contributions.claim: TRACER constructs a medical knowledge graph enriched with severity information from medical literature.
TRACER retrieves severity-weighted progression paths, extracts clinically relevant events from unstructured notes, and augments patient context with similar peer cases.
TRACER provides path-level explanations linking risk estimates to literature-backed logic and specific textual evidence.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV report up to a 28.5% Macro F1 increase for mortality prediction over state-of-the-art baselines.
Experiments report up to a 19.7% increase for readmission prediction over state-of-the-art baselines.
TRACER produces transparent path-level explanations for clinicians.

narrative_sequence.summary: Clinical risk prediction requires augmenting EHR records with heterogeneous external knowledge.
Existing methods miss severity, treatment response, and nuanced progression, partly because of sparsity and limited use of clinical notes.
TRACER combines a severity-enriched medical knowledge graph, severity-weighted trajectory retrieval, note-event extraction, and peer-case context augmentation.
Experiments on two MIMIC datasets report gains over state-of-the-art baselines for mortality and readmission prediction.
The framework supplies path-level explanations based on literature-backed logic and textual evidence.

source_observation.claim: Combining structured severity-aware knowledge with extracted information from clinical notes and similar cases is associated with reported improvements in clinical risk prediction.

interpretation.claim: Risk prediction systems may benefit from integrating heterogeneous evidence sources while preserving progression and severity information.

application.claim: For related clinical prediction tasks, consider representing disease trajectories and retrieving severity-weighted evidence alongside structured patient records.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which individual component causes the reported gains.

source_observation.claim: TRACER reports transparent explanations that connect risk estimates to literature-backed paths and textual evidence.

interpretation.claim: Explanation mechanisms can make retrieved clinical reasoning artifacts inspectable by domain experts.

application.claim: Clinical prediction interfaces may expose the supporting paths and note evidence behind individual risk estimates.

exception.claim: The abstract does not report whether clinicians validated the explanations or whether they improve decisions.

unknowns: No architectural or training details are provided.
No dataset splits, cohort definitions, baseline identities, or statistical significance information are provided.
No ablation results isolate the effects of severity grounding, note extraction, peer cases, or retrieval augmentation.
No details are provided about explanation evaluation or clinical utility.
